Subject: Transfer addendum redlines (DPA) — MediSys comments attached

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for sharing the MSA and order form draft. Our legal team reviewed the DPA and attached a set of redlines focused on the transfer impact and processor/processor roles. Key asks from our side:

- Clarify subprocessors: we need a clear subprocessor notification window (we've proposed 30 days).
- SCCs baseline: include the EU Commission standard clauses reference in the DPA schedule and confirm which controller-to-processor set you're adopting.
- Transfer impact addendum: there are carve-outs requested around training data and model derivatives — see section 4.2 in the attached.
- Audit evidence: procurement requested an inventory of where data may leave the EEA and any persistent backups.

I'm copying procurement for any commercial constraints. Please route these to your privacy/legal folks and let us know a realistic timeline for a consolidated response. For speed, we've attached a tracked-redline Word file (MediSys_DPA_Redlines_20280524.docx) and flagged the high-priority items.

Would appreciate an initial read by end of day tomorrow if possible — we have a deadline for procurement approval the week after next.

Regards,
Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement
MediSys Ltd.

Hi Elena — thanks for the redlines and the clear priority flags.

High-level plan from our side:
1) Ben and Lauren will review the specific clause-level redlines and come back with a consolidated proposal on the notification window, SCC language, and the transfer impact carve-outs.
2) Karthik will assess the technical evidence we can provide about EEA residency, backups, and subprocessor routing.
3) I'll coordinate internal alignment and sync with your procurement team on timelines/cutover.

Quick notes: we typically operate with a 14–30 day subprocessor notice window depending on the deployment (hosted vs dedicated). For the SCCs, we use the EC controller-to-processor clauses and include a transfer impact addendum when region-specific restrictions apply; we'll confirm the exact clause set we intend to adopt.

Ben/Lauren/Karthik — can you triage and aim to provide a consolidated comment set by EOD Friday (25 May)? That would give me time to prepare a mutual action plan for Elena's procurement deadline.

Thanks,

Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Transfer addendum redlines (DPA) — MediSys comments attached

Hi all — reviewed the MediSys redlines and proposed an internal compromise matrix. Summary of our responses (high priority items):

1) Subprocessor notice/window — MediSys requested 30 days. Our standard is 14 days for hosted services, 30 days for Dedicated/Private deployments. Proposal: accept 30 days for this order form (MediSys is EEA-only) and add a short clause allowing shorter notice in emergency situations with post-event notice (security incidents).

2) SCCs — we'll adopt the EC Controller-to-Processor Clauses (2010/2021 stack) and commit to including the SCC schedule in the executed DPA. We'll add explicit language in the DPA schedule confirming the controller/processor mapping and the transfer-impact addendum as an exhibit.

3) Training data & model derivatives carve-out — we will not accept broad ownership claims over model weights. Suggest specific language: Redwood will not use customer PII for model training without explicit written consent; aggregated/anonymous telemetry may be used for product improvement, described in Appendix B with examples and opt-out mechanics.

4) Evidence & backups — Karthik, can you prepare a one-pager inventory of EEA residency, subprocessor regions, and backup retention (S3 snapshot policy + geographic replication) that we can attach to the DPA? Procurement is asking for it.

5) Audit rights — MediSys requests on-site audit rights. Offer: virtual audit with audit logs and scope-limited SOC2 evidence; if MediSys requires on-site audits, we need to discuss timing and costs.

Attached: Redwood_Response_DPA_Consolidated_20280525.docx (proposed tracked redlines), and a short summary PDF.

Next steps:
- Karthik to deliver the technical inventory by EOD Monday 28 May.
- Lauren to draft the SCC schedule language and the training-data appendix.
- Nikhil to confirm commercial sign-off path and whether procurement will accept virtual audit.

Ben Carter
Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Response_DPA_Consolidated_20280525.docx

Ben / Nikhil — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the pragmatic compromises. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal:

- 30-day notice for subprocessors is acceptable. We appreciate the emergency exception language.
- SCC schedule: please share the proposed schedule and the controller/processor mapping as a document (not embedded text). Procurement needs the schedule to be attached to the contract package for their internal reviewers.
- Training-data appendix: the team would like the examples you mentioned and a mechanism for us to opt out of any telemetry-based training.
- Audit: Virtual audit and SOC2 artifacts are the preferred route; if on-site is ever required we'll circle back on cost/resourcing.

Can you send the proposed DPA schedule & the technical inventory by EOD Monday (28 May)? If we can get those two items and a final tracked DPA we can route to Legal & Procurement for signoff next week.

If helpful, happy to do a 30-minute call Monday morning to walk procurement through the inventory.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Procurement
MediSys Ltd.
